examples.en: I went to the memorial hall with my family on the weekend.
There are many old photos inside the memorial hall.
This memorial hall has no admission fee.
The guide slowly explained the memorial hall to us.

examples.ko: 학교 근처에 새로 생긴 기념관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a newly opened memorial hall near the school.
I am waiting for the bus to the memorial hall.

explain: '세종대왕기념관'처럼 사람이나 사건 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 여러 종류의 물건을 모아 보여 주는 곳은 보통 '박물관'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It attaches to the name of a person or event, as in 'Sejong the Great Memorial Hall'. A place that shows many kinds of objects is usually called a 'bakmulgwan' (museum).

examples.en: The child's eyes widened in surprise.
I was speechless with astonishment.
Surprise and joy rushed in all at once.
This result was a surprise to everyone.
The surprise soon turned into laughter.
The news gave a great surprise.

explain: '놀라다'를 명사로 만든 말이에요. '놀라움을 주다', '놀라움을 금치 못하다'처럼 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '놀랐어요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 결과를 보고 모두가 놀라움을 금치 못했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 놀라서 놀란 마음을 감추기 어렵다는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression meaning one is so surprised that it is hard to hide the feeling. You see it in news and writing.
phrases.en_equiv: be unable to contain one's astonishment

explain_en: It is the noun form of '놀라다' (to be surprised). It often appears in writing and news, as in '놀라움을 주다' and '놀라움을 금치 못하다'. In speech, people say '놀랐어요'.

examples.en: The melodrama I watched yesterday was really sad.
I like melodramas more than action.
The lead of this melodrama is a famous actor.
Melodramas usually feature love stories.

examples.ko: 멜로드라마 속 장면 같은 일이 생겼어요!
examples.en: Something like a scene from a melodrama happened!
My parents watch melodramas too on weekends.

explain: 줄여서 '멜로'라고도 해요. 사랑과 이별을 다룬 드라마나 영화를 가리켜요. 웃음이 중심인 '로맨틱 코미디'와는 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is often shortened to '멜로'. It refers to dramas and films about love and parting. People distinguish it from a 'romantic comedy', which centers on laughs.

examples.en: At the restaurant, the server brought a wet towel first.
I applied a hot wet towel to my stiff shoulder.
Sorry, could I have another wet towel?

examples.ko: 물수건이 차가워서 더운 날에 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: The wet towel is cold, so it's perfect on a hot day.
Please bring me just one wet towel.
We first serve guests a wet towel and water.

explain: 식당에서 손을 닦으라고 주는 젖은 수건을 말해요. 포장된 '물티슈'와는 달라요. 뜨겁게 하거나 차갑게 해서 얼굴·몸에 대는 용도로도 써요.
explain_en: It is the damp towel given at restaurants for wiping your hands. It differs from packaged '물티슈' (wet wipes). It can also be heated or chilled and pressed on the face or body.

examples.en: I went sea fishing with my father on the weekend.

examples.ko: 바다낚시는 배를 타고 나가야 해서 멀미가 걱정돼요.
examples.en: Sea fishing means going out on a boat, so I worry about seasickness.

examples.ko: 바다낚시 갈 때는 선크림을 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: I always bring sunscreen when I go sea fishing.
The wind is strong today, so sea fishing was canceled.

examples.ko: 처음 간 바다낚시에서 큰 물고기를 잡았어요.
examples.en: On my first sea fishing trip, I caught a big fish.

examples.ko: 바다낚시도 좋지만 저는 민물낚시가 더 편해요.
examples.en: Sea fishing is good too, but I find freshwater fishing more comfortable.

explain: 반대는 '민물낚시'예요. '바다낚시를 가다/하다'처럼 말하고, 낚시를 가는 이야기에서는 '가다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '민물낚시' (freshwater fishing). You say '바다낚시를 가다/하다', and when talking about the trip, '가다' is used a lot.

examples.en: I put the papers into a binder and organized them.
The binder is thick, so it doesn't fit in my bag.
I went to the stationery store to buy a new binder.

examples.ko: 수업 자료는 파란 바인더 안에 있어요.
examples.en: The class materials are in the blue binder.
If you bind them in a binder, the papers won't scatter.
The teacher said we need a binder.

explain: '파일'은 얇은 서류 보관 케이스를 가리킬 때 쓰고, '바인더'는 고리가 있어서 구멍 뚫은 종이를 끼워 두는 두꺼운 것을 가리킬 때 써요. 학교나 회사에서 자료를 모을 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: 파일 is used for a thin case that holds papers, while 바인더 is the thicker one with rings where you clip hole-punched paper. People use it to collect materials at school or work.

examples.en: The teacher told me to write a letter of reflection and bring it.

examples.ko: 반성문은 변명보다 잘못을 인정하는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In a letter of reflection, admitting your fault matters more than excuses.

examples.ko: 친구와 싸운 뒤 반성문 한 장을 썼어요.
examples.en: After fighting with a friend, I wrote a one-page letter of reflection.

examples.ko: 반성문이 너무 짧다고 다시 쓰라고 했어요.
examples.en: They said my letter of reflection was too short and told me to rewrite it.
My younger sibling held out, saying they didn't even want to write the apology letter.
In the letter of reflection, I also wrote what I'd do from now on.

explain: 잘못을 돌아보고 쓰는 글이에요. '반성문을 쓰다/내다/제출하다'로 말해요. 회사에서 비슷한 글은 '시말서'라고 하고, 남에게 사과하는 글은 '사과문'이에요.
explain_en: It is writing in which you reflect on your wrongdoing. You say '반성문을 쓰다/내다/제출하다'. A similar document at a company is a '시말서', and a letter apologizing to others is a '사과문'.

examples.en: I went to the sea at night and listened to the waves.
Unlike in the daytime, the sea at night is very quiet.
Walking while looking at the night sea calms my mind.
The wind blowing from the night sea is cool.
The night sea with lights reflected on it was really beautiful.
We set off fireworks at the sea at night with friends.

explain: '밤바다' 하면 조용하고 낭만적인 분위기를 떠올려요. 보통 '보러 가다, 걷다, 바라보다'처럼 풍경을 즐기는 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: '밤바다' brings to mind a quiet, romantic mood. It's usually used with verbs of enjoying the scenery, like '보러 가다', '걷다' and '바라보다'.

examples.en: This baseball bat is too heavy.
The player held the bat and waited for the ball.
Bats are made of wood or metal.
The ball hit the bat and flew far away.
The child hit the ball hard with the bat.

examples.ko: 글러브뿐 아니라 배트도 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: I need to buy a new bat, not just a glove.

explain: 야구 방망이를 '방망이'라고도 하지만 야구에서는 '배트'를 더 자주 써요. 동물 박쥐는 영어로 bat이지만 한국어로는 '박쥐'라고 해요.
explain_en: A baseball bat can also be called '방망이', but in baseball '배트' is more common. The animal bat is '박쥐' in Korean, not '배트'.

examples.en: This animal is protected by Korean law.
Personal information is being kept safe.
Our cultural properties must be well protected.

examples.ko: 보호된 숲에서는 나무를 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut trees in a protected forest.
It is dangerous if children are not properly protected.

examples.ko: 이 해변은 바다거북 때문에 보호될 거예요.
examples.en: This beach will be protected because of the sea turtles.

explain: '보호하다'는 지키는 쪽이고, '보호되다'는 지켜지는 상태예요. 법·제도·환경 이야기에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '지켜지다'가 더 구어적이에요. '보호자'는 아이나 환자를 돌보는 어른을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '보호하다' is the side protecting; '보호되다' is the state of being protected. It appears in talk of laws, systems and the environment, while '지켜지다' is more colloquial. '보호자' refers to the adult looking after a child or a patient.

examples.en: The dawn sky was tinged with a pale pink.
In spring the cherry blossoms take on a pink tint.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 아기 볼이 분홍빛이에요.
examples.en: The baby was outside on a cold day, so its cheeks are pink.
You look bright in that pink dress.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 노을이 분홍빛에서 보랏빛으로 변했어요.
examples.en: At sunset the glow changed from pink to purple.
The pink of that flower gets deeper and deeper.

explain: '분홍색'은 색 이름 자체를 말할 때 쓰고, '분홍빛'은 하늘, 볼, 노을처럼 은은하게 번지거나 감도는 색에 잘 어울려요. '붉은빛', '보랏빛'처럼 '-빛'으로 끝나는 짝말이 많아요.
explain_en: '분홍색' simply names the color, while '분홍빛' suits a pink that softly spreads or glows, such as in the sky, cheeks or sunset. There are many matching words ending in '-빛', like '붉은빛' and '보랏빛'.

examples.en: Our cat is a calico, with three colors.
This cloth is woven in three colors.
I made a bracelet with three-colored thread.

examples.ko: 빨강, 노랑, 파랑 삼색을 섞어 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: I mix the three colors red, yellow and blue to paint.
A three-colored flag is waving in the wind.
I bought clothes where the three colors go well together.

explain: 고양이 털 색이 세 가지면 '삼색 고양이'라고 해요. '삼색 실', '삼색 볼펜'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 색 세 개를 풀어서 말할 때는 '세 가지 색'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A cat whose fur has three colors is called a '삼색 고양이'. You can put it before another noun, as in '삼색 실' or '삼색 볼펜'. When you spell it out, you can also say '세 가지 색'.

examples.en: The speaker is too loud.
I played music through the speaker.
I bought a new Bluetooth speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: The speaker seems broken, since there is no sound.
I connect my phone to the speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커는 방 구석에 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is better to put the speaker in a corner of the room.

explain: '스피커폰으로 통화하다'처럼 전화 소리를 밖으로 내는 기능에도 써요. 이어폰은 귀에 꽂고, 스피커는 밖으로 소리를 내요.
explain_en: It is also used for the phone function that plays call sound aloud, as in 'seupikeophoneuro tonghwahada'. Earphones go in your ears; a speaker sends sound out into the room.

examples.en: There is trust between us.

examples.ko: 신뢰를 얻으려면 약속을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: To earn trust you have to keep your promises.

examples.ko: 작은 거짓말 하나로 신뢰에 금이 갔어요.
examples.en: One small lie put a crack in the trust.

examples.ko: 한 번 깨진 신뢰는 다시 쌓기 어려워요.
examples.en: Trust that has been broken once is hard to rebuild.

examples.ko: 신뢰할 수 있는 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with someone I can trust.
Friendships are held together by trust.

explain: '믿음'과 뜻이 가깝지만, 신뢰는 회사·뉴스·정치처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 더 잘 써요. 친구나 가족에게는 '믿음'이나 '믿다'를 더 자주 말해요. '신뢰를 얻다', '신뢰를 쌓다', '신뢰가 깨지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to 믿음, but 신뢰 suits slightly stiff settings such as business, news, and politics. With friends and family, people more often say 믿음 or 믿다. It pairs with fixed verbs: 신뢰를 얻다, 신뢰를 쌓다, 신뢰가 깨지다.

examples.en: I went to watch an ice hockey game in winter.

examples.ko: 아이스하키는 얼음 위에서 퍽을 쳐서 해요.
examples.en: In ice hockey, you hit a puck on the ice.
My younger sibling is learning ice hockey.
Ice hockey is fun, so I watch it every week.
Everyone cheered when a goal was scored in the ice hockey game.
I am trying both ice hockey and skating for the first time.

explain: '하키'만 말하면 땅 위에서 하는 필드하키를 뜻할 수 있어서, 얼음 위에서 하는 경기는 앞에 '아이스'를 붙여요.
explain_en: Saying 하키 alone can mean the field version played on grass, so the game on ice gets 아이스 in front.

examples.ko: 나가기 전에 거울로 내 앞모습을 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before going out, I checked my front view in the mirror.

examples.ko: 앞모습은 멋있는데 뒷모습은 어딘가 피곤해 보여요.
examples.en: He looks cool from the front, but from behind he looks somehow tired.

examples.ko: 사진 속 앞모습만 보고는 누군지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I couldn't tell who it was just from the front view in the photo.
From the front, he looks a lot like his father.
The front of the building was pretty, so I took a photo.

examples.ko: 뒷모습만 보고 아는 사람인 줄 알았는데 앞모습을 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I thought it was someone I knew from the back, but I was startled when I saw the front.

explain: 반대말은 '뒷모습'이에요. 사람의 얼굴이나 앞쪽 모양, 건물의 앞쪽 모양에 써요. '뒷모습'은 쓸쓸하거나 믿음직한 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '뒷모습' (back view). It is used for a person's face or front appearance and for the front of a building. '뒷모습' is often used to describe a lonely or reliable feeling.

examples.en: Palm trees stand in a row on the beach.
I rested for a moment in the shade of a palm tree.
They planted palm trees in the hotel garden.
The palm leaves are swaying in the wind.
Many palm trees grow in tropical regions.

examples.ko: 그림 속 야자수가 휴양지 느낌을 줘요.
examples.en: The palm tree in the picture gives a resort feel.

explain: '야자나무'라고도 해요. 야자수는 바다, 휴가, 열대 같은 느낌을 떠올리게 해서 그림이나 인테리어에서도 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is also called '야자나무'. Palm trees bring to mind the sea, vacations and the tropics, so they are often used in pictures and interior decoration.

examples.en: I stuffed some clothes loosely into the travel bag.
Clothes are scattered on the floor.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 안 입는 옷가지를 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I sorted out the clothes I don't wear.
I grabbed just a few pieces of clothing and left.
Please bring me the clothes to wash.
I dry clothes soaked by rain separately.

explain: '옷' 한 벌이 아니라 이것저것 여러 종류의 옷을 가볍게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '옷가지 몇 벌'처럼 말하고, 옷 하나를 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요. 짐을 싸거나 빨래, 정리할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it to loosely group several pieces of clothing, not one garment. You say things like '옷가지 몇 벌', and you don't use it for a single item. It often comes up when packing, doing laundry or tidying.

examples.en: In autumn the ginkgo leaves turn yellow.
I walked stepping on the ginkgo leaves piled on the ground.
I made a bookmark out of a ginkgo leaf.
The color of the ginkgo leaves is really pretty.
A ginkgo leaf is shaped like a fan.
Sunlight shines on the yellow ginkgo leaves and it's dazzling.

explain: '은행'은 은행나무와 열매를 가리키기도 하고 'bank'와 소리가 같지만, 문맥으로 쉽게 구분돼요. 가을 단풍 이야기에서 '노란 은행잎'이 자주 나와요. [은행닙]으로 발음해요.
explain_en: '은행' can mean the ginkgo tree and its nut, and it sounds like 'bank', but the context makes it easy to tell. '노란 은행잎' (yellow ginkgo leaves) often comes up when talking about autumn colors. It is pronounced [은행닙].

examples.en: I feel deep respect for my parents.
My respect toward my teacher grew little by little.

examples.ko: 존경심은 말보다 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You should show respect through actions rather than words.

examples.ko: 그는 존경심으로 가득한 눈으로 할아버지를 바라봤어요.
examples.en: He looked at his grandfather with eyes full of respect.
It was a small action that came from respect.
It is behavior with neither respect nor manners.

explain: '호기심', '애국심'처럼 '-심'은 마음을 나타내요. '존경심을 느끼다', '존경심을 갖다'처럼 써요. 사람을 대할 때는 '선생님을 존경해요'라고 동사로 말하고, 다른 사람의 의견이나 선택을 인정할 때는 '존중'을 써요.
explain_en: As in '호기심' and '애국심', the '-심' part shows a feeling in the mind. It goes with '존경심을 느끼다' and '존경심을 갖다'. About a person you can use the verb, as in '선생님을 존경해요', and for accepting someone's opinion or choice you use '존중'.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 편리성이 가장 큰 장점이에요.
examples.en: This app's biggest strength is its convenience.
If you only consider convenience, a card is better than cash.
I think convenience is more important than price.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑의 편리성 덕분에 시장에 잘 안 가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the convenience of online shopping, I rarely go to the market.
The convenience is good, but the price is too high.
You have to take care of both convenience and safety.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '편해요'나 '편리해요'라고 말하고, '편리성'은 제품이나 서비스를 비교하거나 설명할 때 써요. '-성'이 붙은 말이라 '안전성', '효율성'과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '편해요' or '편리해요', while '편리성' is used when comparing or describing products and services. It ends in '-성', so it often appears alongside words like '안전성' (safety) and '효율성' (efficiency).

examples.en: If you read a lot of books, your expressive ability grows.

examples.ko: 한국어 표현력을 키우고 싶어서 일기를 써요.
examples.en: I want to build my Korean expression skills, so I write a diary.

examples.ko: 표현력은 연습하면 누구나 좋아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can get better at expressing themselves with practice.
To give a good presentation, expressive skill matters too.
I was surprised by the child's expressive ability.

examples.ko: 저는 표현력과 이해력을 함께 기르고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to develop both expressiveness and comprehension.

explain: '표현력이 좋다', '표현력이 풍부하다', '표현력이 늘다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말 '어휘력'은 아는 단어의 양에 가깝고, '표현력'은 생각이나 느낌을 말과 글로 잘 나타내는 힘이에요.
explain_en: It goes with phrases like '표현력이 좋다' and '표현력이 늘다'. The related word '어휘력' is closer to how many words you know, while '표현력' is how well you put thoughts and feelings into speech or writing.

examples.en: Korean has many ways of expressing politeness.

examples.ko: 같은 뜻도 표현법에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
examples.en: Even the same meaning feels different depending on how it is expressed.
I learned ways to express feelings from this book.
Ways of greeting differ a little from country to country.

examples.ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 공손한 표현법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me a polite way to ask for a favor.
Please explain it again in simpler words.

explain: '표현'이 말이나 글로 나타낸 것 자체라면, '표현법'은 그것을 나타내는 방식을 말해요. '감정 표현법', '인사 표현법'처럼 앞에 주제를 붙여서 자주 써요.
explain_en: While '표현' is the thing expressed itself, '표현법' is the way of expressing it. It is often used with a topic in front, like '감정 표현법' (ways to express feelings) or '인사 표현법' (ways to greet).

examples.en: Small wildflowers have bloomed along the road.
The children picked wildflowers and made flower rings.
I felt spring in a tiny wildflower.
The walking path is full of wildflowers.

examples.ko: 풀꽃 이름을 하나도 몰라서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know any of the wildflower names, so I took photos.

examples.ko: 풀꽃은 작지만 자세히 보면 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: Wildflowers are small, but they are really pretty up close.

explain: 꽃집에서 파는 꽃이나 화단의 꽃과 달리, 들이나 길가에서 저절로 자라는 작은 꽃을 말할 때 써요. '들꽃'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 '풀꽃'은 풀처럼 작고 소박한 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike florist flowers or garden flowers, it refers to small flowers that grow by themselves in fields or by the road. It is close to '들꽃', but '풀꽃' sounds smaller and more modest, like the grass itself.
